rationale_letter: Re: Readmission Claim RM_04 - Determination of Relatedness to Prior Index Admission MR_04 Dear Provider, This office has completed a medical review of readmission claim RM_04 and the paired index claim MR_04 per the Lake Ontario Health Cooperative Readmission Review Guideline. We have determined that the readmission is clinically related to the prior index admission and therefore meets the payer's definition of a Readmission Finding under Section B1 ("same or related condition"). Basis for Determination: - Policy: Lake Ontario's guideline specifies a 30-day review window and requires a Finding when the readmission diagnosis is the same as, or clinically related to, the condition or procedure treated during the prior stay (Lake Ontario Readmission Review Guideline, Review Window: 30 days; Section B1) (evidence: guideline text). - Timing: The index stay discharged 05/23/2026 and the readmission began 06/13/2026, which is within the payer's 30-day review window. - Clinical linkage: The readmission discharge summary documents Infection and inflammatory reaction due to internal fixation device of left femur (T84.612A) as the principal diagnosis and explicitly states this was a direct infectious complication of the orthopedic hardware implanted during the index trauma admission. The index discharge documentation records intramedullary femoral fixation during the index hospitalization. (Evidence: readmission DISCHARGE SUMMARY; index DISCHARGE / TRANSFER SUMMARY.) - Exclusions: The guideline's exclusions (e.g., direct transfers, admissions that began as SNF/IRF/LTAC) do not apply: the readmission presented from home 7 days after discharge from the IRF (not a direct facility-to-facility transfer), so the exclusion for admissions that originated as SNF/IRF/LTAC does not negate the Finding. Conclusion and Action: Accordingly, under Lake Ontario Health Cooperative's Readmission Review Guideline, readmission RM_04 is a Finding under Section B1 ("same or related condition") because it documents a direct infectious complication of surgical hardware placed during the index admission MR_04 within the payer's 30-day review window. Please record this audit determination in your administrative/appeals systems. If you dispute this determination, provide supporting clinical documentation that rebuts the clinical linkage (for example, evidence the infection arose from an unrelated new injury or that the hardware was placed after the index stay). Sincerely, Clinical Claims Audit Team Cited evidence (representative): Lake Ontario Readmission Review Guideline (Section B1; Review Window 30 days), RM_04 Discharge Summary (Clinical Relationship and Diagnostic Concordance), MR_04 Discharge / Transfer Summary (index procedure and discharge date).
